text:
alex: FYI canary in eu-west-1 failing after CNI 1.12 rolled. GPU nodegroup pods stuck ContainerCreating with AttachVolume.WaitForAttach and ENI limits spiking :eyes:
ops-bot: Alert: autoscaler modified launch_template: block_device_mappings changed. Associated PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482
mira: can you paste the pod describe / events?
alex: `kubectl -n ml describe pod gpu-worker-7f6c9` shows `failed to assign IPv4 address` and "no available addresses in subnet" in the events. Node allocations show ENI count near max on several instances.
sam: sounds like we hit AWS ENI per-instance limits. Our mixed instance policy includes smaller g5/g4dn variants — some have low ENI capacity. We should pin to g5.4xlarge (higher ENI) or request quota bumps.
raj: terraform plan shows drift: launch_template.user_data differs (base64 blob). Looks like autoscaler or a bootstrap change mutated user_data outside gitops. `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan` highlights the diff.
jen: the helm canary for the CNI chart failed too — values had `nodeSelector: { "kubernetes.io/arch": "amd64,gpu" }` which is invalid and broke affinity. Need to split nodeAffinity for gpu nodes.
mira: for immediate mitigation can we scale up a different AZ or region nodegroup to take critical pods? eu-west-1 quotas are tight right now.
alex: @jen @sam can you open a small PR to revert the CNI change in the canary and add a post-upgrade check for ENI availability?
sam: opening PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/483. I'll add a preflight job in the gitops pipeline that runs a quick ENI check: `aws ec2 describe-instance-types --instance-types g5.4xlarge --query \"NetworkInfo.EnaSupport,NetworkInfo.MaximumNetworkInterfaces\"`
raj: longer term we should guard terraform: add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [launch_template[0].user_data] }` while we trace the source of mutation, but let's document it clearly so we don't mask real config drift.
jen: on flux/helm-controller side I'll change the canary strategy to `maxUnavailable: 1` and add a `post-install` job that runs `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath=\"{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.status.allocatable.alpha\.kubernetes\.io/~eni}\n\"` (will stub this properly) to ensure ENI capacity remains before promoting.
ops-bot: Incident annotated: #INC-2026-03-17-ENI-QUOTA. Affected: eu-west-1 gpu pool. Oncall: @mira.
mira: I'm opening a support ticket with AWS to check soft quota bump for ENI per instance type + request more g5.4xlarge quota in eu-west-1. Also checking VPC IP pool utilization.
alex: quick cost note — pinning to larger instance types will increase steady-state cost; add a note to the infra-cost channel to discuss committed reserved capacity vs on-demand bursts.
jen: small follow-up: helm chart values cleanup PR incoming to fix the nodeSelector/affinity confusion, will include a unit test for values parsing.
sam: added a preflight step to the GitHub Actions job that gates the helm upgrade in canary: runs `aws ec2 describe-addresses` and a tiny python script to assert available ENIs > threshold.
alex: Summary action items: 1) revert CNI upgrade in eu-west-1 canary (PR 483), 2) add preflight ENI check in gitops pipeline, 3) pin GPU instance types in nodegroup to high-ENI flavors, 4) add terraform ignore_changes for launch_template.user_data short-term, 5) open AWS support quota request. Assigning owners in the PRs. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Deploy job for PR 483 queued to canary eu-west-1. Will run after CI checks pass.
